name: Panta Detroit CPC Diagnostic Reference
source: User-supplied Scribd CPC Codes1 reference, cross-checked against publicly available Detroit/DTNA CPC material
usage_note: Curated diagnostic knowledge, not a verbatim reproduction. CPC faults must be interpreted by exact Detroit generation, SPN/FMI, vehicle configuration and current service information. Do not condemn a CPC or connected component from a code alone.

documents.title: Detroit Common Powertrain Controller diagnostic role
documents.summary: The CPC is the vehicle-side Detroit controller. It receives driver and vehicle inputs such as accelerator-pedal and engine-brake requests, exchanges information with the MCM and other ECUs over J1939/proprietary data links, and stores application-specific vehicle parameters. CPC complaints can therefore involve pedal inputs, cruise/PTO logic, vehicle parameters, network communication, power/ground or CPC internal faults.

documents.title: CPC SPN 91 accelerator pedal position faults
documents.summary: Detroit CPC SPN 91 is associated with accelerator-pedal position input. CPC troubleshooting literature distinguishes high- and low-voltage/circuit conditions by FMI. Diagnose reference voltage, signal, ground, connector and wiring integrity and compare pedal channels where applicable before replacing the pedal or CPC.

documents.title: CPC SPN 168 battery and supply-voltage faults
documents.summary: CPC SPN 168 represents battery/supply-voltage related faults. Detroit procedures commonly direct technicians to resolve SPN 168 voltage faults before diagnosing communication faults because unstable CPC/MCM/ACM power can create secondary network codes. Verify batteries, charging, CPC feeds, grounds and voltage drop under the relevant condition.

documents.title: CPC SPN 247 MCM engine-hours data faults
documents.summary: Detroit CPC SPN 247 can report MCM engine-hours data higher than expected, lower than expected, or not received/stopped arriving depending on FMI. Detroit literature notes these faults can occur after CPC or MCM programming when internal hour data/clocks do not agree. Check programming history and module communication before hardware replacement.

documents.title: CPC SPN 609 controller faults
documents.summary: SPN 609 is a CPC/controller fault family. The FMI and Detroit generation determine whether the reported condition involves internal hardware/software, temperature or another controller condition. Do not treat every SPN 609 as automatic CPC replacement; verify power/ground, programming/configuration and the exact Detroit diagnostic procedure.

documents.title: CPC SPN 615 transmission J1939 DM1 message missing
documents.summary: Detroit CPC SPN 615 FMI 9 indicates the J1939 DM1 message from the transmission is missing. Detroit troubleshooting checks for battery-voltage faults first, related CAN faults, recent CPC programming/configuration, and which vehicle modules are configured and communicating. A missing message does not by itself prove the transmission controller is defective.

documents.title: Detroit CPC/MCM powertrain CAN communication faults
documents.summary: Detroit SPN 625 communication faults can involve the powertrain CAN relationship between CPC, MCM and other modules. Water intrusion, damaged connectors, open/shorted CAN wiring, termination, loss of module power/ground or configuration/programming issues can prevent communication. Resolve supply-voltage faults and inspect network integrity before condemning modules.

documents.title: CPC SPN 701 digital-output / Top 2 lockout solenoid fault family
documents.summary: On applicable Detroit CPC4 configurations, SPN 701 FMI 5 identifies an open circuit associated with the Top 2 lockout-solenoid CPC output. Detroit documentation warns that CPC digital-output SPNs can overlap numbers used for MCM faults, so identify which module logged the fault before diagnosing the circuit.

documents.title: CPC SPN 3510 sensor supply voltage faults
documents.summary: Detroit CPC SPN 3510 includes sensor-supply voltage faults. For applicable systems, low-voltage diagnosis can involve isolating the accelerator-pedal circuit and CPC connector wiring to find shorts or opens. Shared reference-voltage faults should be diagnosed as a circuit before multiple sensors or the CPC are replaced.

documents.title: Detroit CPC communication diagnostic priority
documents.summary: For CPC/MCM/ACM communication complaints, first capture all module faults and determine which modules are actually offline. Address battery/supply-voltage faults, check recent programming or configuration changes, inspect CPC/MCM/ACM connectors for corrosion/water/unseated terminals, then test the CAN network and module power/grounds using the applicable Detroit procedure. Multiple network codes often share one root cause.
